primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'tier': 'model classification level (sonnet, haiku)', '$/Mtok': 'cost per million tokens'}
primitives.assumptions: Model tiers are fixed, cost is invariant across runs.

primitives.name: Surface Cost Savings
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$/Mtok (act.)': 'actual cost per million tokens', '$/Mtok (rec.)': 'recommenced cost per million tokens', 'Savings': 'percentage difference between act. and rec. costs'}
primitives.assumptions: Costs are known, savings computed as percentage delta.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime of zero or negative savings due to cost inflation.

layer2.mapping: Drives GSE cost optimization decisions via savings metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage savings or loss per surface.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives form a layered system where static cost-quality assessment provides deterministic baseline metrics, active model tiering enables dynamic cost allocation, and surface cost savings define optimization targets. The system assumes static inference and deterministic rubrics, enabling Bayesian quality tracking without live feedback. Dualities emerge in cost consistency vs. savings variability. Failure modes include misalignment between static rubrics and evolving prompt effectiveness, or incorrect model tiering leading to suboptimal cost-savings. The system's robustness depends on accurate vendor-sourced cost data and consistent prompt design.
